subject: Automotive & EVs
title: Weight Distribution
description: A short lesson to help you apply Weight Distribution.

hook.text: Where weight sits in a car determines how it turns, brakes, and accelerates.

buildup.text: A front-heavy car tends to push wide in corners, called understeer—the nose drifts outward.

discovery.text: A rear-heavy car can swing its tail out, called oversteer—exciting but harder to control.

twist.text: The ideal is 50/50 front-to-rear. BMW engineered this balance for decades as a brand identity.

climax.text: EVs naturally sit low because heavy batteries line the floor—giving them a very low center of gravity.

punchline.text: Balance is what separates a good car from a great one.
